explanation:
Generated an EXCLURAD input.dat for the pion channel (ivec=2, detected pi+, recoil neutron) using the JeffersonLab pion/exclurad.F code, for the single kinematic point W=1.4 GeV, Q2=0.8 GeV^2, cos(theta*)=0.3, phi*=120 deg. I verified this point is kinematically allowed (the electron scattering angle solves to a valid cos(theta_e) in (-1,1) for the assumed beam momentum, and the pion-CM invariant-mass/momentum radicals in bornkin/sffun are real and positive), so this is not a physically impossible request.

However, the code's read sequence (iphy, ll, bmom, tmom, lepton, ivec, cutv, npoi, then W/Q2/cos*/phi* arrays) requires an incident lepton momentum 'bmom' that is NOT determined by (W, Q2, cos*, phi*) alone. The same exclusive (W,Q2) point can be produced at many different beam energies with different electron scattering angles, and the QED radiative-correction size (through the virtual-photon polarization epsilon in borntest, and through ee1,ee2,pp1,pp2,cos1,cos2 in bornkin/rv2tr which set the real-bremsstrahlung phase space) depends on that choice. The user's request did not specify a beam energy, so this is an underspecified input rather than a physically impossible one.

I did not invent an arbitrary new number: I carried over bmom=1.645 GeV, the only beam momentum given in the code's own README/input.dat example, as a clearly-flagged placeholder (tmom=0 for a fixed target, lepton=1 for electron beam). This choice is kinematically valid for the requested point (electron scattering angle ~51.6 deg, bmom_prime=beam momentum after energy loss to the virtual photon ~0.64 GeV, both physical), but it is almost certainly NOT the actual beam energy used in whatever experiment/proposal the user has in mind. The radiative-correction factors (sig/sib, sib/sibt, asymmetry dd, etc.) reported by exclurad for this input.dat will only be physically meaningful for that experiment if bmom is edited to match the real accelerator beam energy before running. All other settings use the README defaults: iphy=3 (MAID2007), ll=0 (Full calculation, not just factorizable/leading-log), vcut=0.05 (standard inelasticity cut).
